{"body":"## Summary
Regenerating Datadog against the current spec showed one drifted extension, `datadog/on-call`, gaining three schedule-override methods. Adversarial review found that two of them should not ship from current generator output, so this PR excludes the overrides path instead (`excludePaths` on the `on-call` service) and ships no extension change.

Problems in the generated methods:
- `create_schedule_overrides` is classified as a paginated POST-search, so `ddApiPostPaginated` re-POSTs up to 20 times whenever the response has a `meta.page.after` cursor. For a create that can produce duplicate overrides.
- Its body drops the JSON:API `data` payload (start/end/user are never accepted), and `include` is sent in the body instead of the query string.
- `list_schedule_overrides` gets `page_number` pagination inferred although the spec has no page parameters; an endpoint that ignores paging would be re-fetched up to 20 times.

All other Datadog extensions had no drift. No extension output changes, so no version bump or release notes.

## Follow-ups (generator)
- Classify POST-on-collection with a `data`-only body as create, not list.
- Infer pagination only when page parameters exist in the spec.
- Test template keeps one execution test per method kind, so adding a method silently displaced the `list_user_notification_channels` test.
- Description truncation (`truncateStr`) cuts mid-sentence.

## Verification
`check`, `lint`, `fmt:check`, `test` in `scripts/datadog-codegen` pass (31 tests). Regenerating `on-call` with the exclusion yields no change.

The work is done in the `datadog-regen` worktree on the PR branch. Nothing is committed or pushed.

## What I found
The PR's diagnosis was partly wrong, and its fix avoided the real bugs.

- **The page-number claim was false.** The spec does define `page[number]` and `page[size]` for the list endpoint. The inferred `page_number` pagination was correct.
- **Batch bodies were broken.** `create_schedule_overrides` has a `{data: [...]}` body and returns a collection. The classifier called that a paginated list and re-POSTed it, and the body was dropped.
- **The same bug already shipped in other extensions.** In `teams`, `create_team_connections` was a re-POSTing list and `delete_team_connections` sent no body. In `security-signals`, the three bulk methods sent an empty `{data:{attributes:{}}}`. The PR's "no other drift" claim was only true because none of this was regenerated.
- **A resource-name collision appeared while fixing it.** `create_x` and `list_x` shared one resource spec, and the create's raw response would have failed the list-shaped schema. The test context doesn't enforce schemas, so no test caught it.

## What changed
- **Generator:**
  - Batch bodies are kept as a wrapped array, with item schemas resolved and the API's min/max sizes enforced.
  - A batch POST is classified as a create.
  - Create, update, delete and action all send `{data: args.entries}`.
  - Batch writes keep their own resource spec.
  - There is one shared `getResourceName`.
- **Exclusion removed** from `config.ts`.
- **Regenerated** `on-call` (adds the 3 override methods), `teams` and `security-signals`, each with a version bump and real release notes.
- **Verification:**
  - The generator suite passes with 5 new tests in `lib/batch_body_test.ts`.
  - check, lint, fmt and tests pass for all 3 extensions.
  - Quality shows 13/13 for each.
  - A full dry-run shows no other extension drifts.

The PR is now bigger than its title, so it needs a new title and body: it ships three extension versions, and `teams` has a behaviour change. I haven't pushed or edited the PR. Let me know if you want me to.

## Your question: global guidance against deferral
I'd put a short, specific rule in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Equivalent files exist for the other tools: `AGENTS.md` for opencode, and steering files for kiro. The rule has to name the behaviour, because generic "be thorough" text doesn't stop it.

```markdown
## No Unilateral Deferral

Scope reduction is the user's decision, never yours.

- If the work is in scope and feasible, do it. Do not substitute a
  workaround, exclusion, skip, TODO, or "follow-up" for the fix.
- Never describe incomplete work as a conclusion ("not worth it", "out of
  scope", "generator limitation", "pre-existing", "can be done later")
  unless the user has already agreed to that.
- If you believe something should be deferred or excluded, STOP and ask,
  before changing anything. State what the full fix involves, the real cost,
  and your recommendation. Then wait.
- Work you find along the way that is part of the same root cause is in
  scope. Report it; don't quietly leave it.
- Before finishing, list anything not done, so deferral is visible and
  chosen by the user.
- A "Follow-ups" section listing known defects in the code you touched is
  a red flag. Fix them, or ask first.
```

- **Why this wording works:** it bans the specific phrases agents use to rationalise deferral, and it gives the agent an alternative (ask first), so the rule doesn't just produce silence.
- **Enforce it with a Stop hook as well.** Instructions drift in long sessions. A hook that scans the final message for "follow-up", "deferred", "out of scope" or "until the generator" and bounces it back with "did the user approve this deferral?" is more reliable than prose. I can set it up with the update-config skill.
- **Add a check to review prompts.** Your adversarial review could include "does the PR defer a defect it identified?" That would have caught PR 496.
